solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Another image Nasa faked?

indicators.note: a faked image has been doctored, its elements rearranged

explanation.surface: A conspiracy theorist greets another space photo as one more NASA fake.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'Another?' at a bar and the reply is 'same again' — the definition is a request for a repeat drink, not a second picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub idiom: asking for 'another' means ordering a repeat of the drink you just had.

clue.text: Fur coat originally bought in fundraiser?

indicators.note: the original letter of a word is its first

parts.note: a jumble or charity sale raises funds

indicators.note: the letter is placed in the middle of the other word, as something sits in a box

explanation.surface: Someone snapped up a fur coat at a charity sale.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that a sale is only one kind of fundraiser.
explanation.definitionFit: The dark pelt of the marten gives its name both to the fur and to a coat made from it.

clue.text: Mass uprising to flourish under Zapata?

indicators.note: in a down answer, the second piece is written below the first

parts.note: Emiliano Zapata was a revolutionary from Mexico
to flourish a flag is to wave it

explanation.surface: A call for the masses to rise and flourish under the revolutionary Zapata.
explanation.walkthrough: The revolutionary backdrop makes 'uprising' a revolt; it is a stadium crowd standing up in turn. Zapata is only an example of a Mexican, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A playful literal reading: a stadium crowd rising section by section is a mass of people going up.

clue.text: Frightened, with force succumbing to Irish attack

indicators.note: one who succumbs gives way

parts.note: IR = Irish; it replaces the F

explanation.surface: A frightened force gives way before an Irish assault.
explanation.walkthrough: AFRAID with its F swapped for IR becomes A-IR-RAID.
explanation.definitionFit: A specific kind standing for the general: a bombing from aircraft is one form of attack.

clue.text: Brief account, charmingly old-fashioned

parts.note: AC = account, as on bank statements

explanation.surface: A short story told in a pleasantly dated style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief account' reads as a noun phrase, a short story; 'Brief' is really the verb, to inform.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: both mean to give someone the facts they need.

clue.text: Acid murderer keeling over at home

indicators.note: something that keels over ends up the other way round

explanation.surface: A murderer who used acid collapses at home.
explanation.walkthrough: The acid-bath murderer is a real figure of tabloid crime, which makes 'Acid murderer' read as one phrase; the definition is 'Acid' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: this B vitamin is chemically nicotinic acid.

clue.text: Mount's in poetic region, some would say

indicators.note: flags that the answer is how the words are spoken

parts.note: clime is a poetic word for a region

explanation.surface: A mountain sits in some romantic, poetically named land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' looks like a noun, a mountain in that region; it is the verb, to go up. The B is silent, which is why only 'some' would say it this way.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: to mount stairs or a hill is to go up them.

clue.text: Who will investigate singer getting run down?

indicators.note: the R (run) is moved further down the word

parts.note: a crooner is a singer of sentimental songs

explanation.surface: Police wonder who will look into a singer being knocked over by a car.
explanation.walkthrough: CROONER with its R shifted one place down, as a down answer reads, gives CORONER. A coroner does investigate a death such as a run-down singer's, so the surface nearly defines itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A coroner is the official who investigates sudden or suspicious deaths.

clue.text: Sick heading removed from poster

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, here taken away

parts.note: a bill is a poster, as in 'Stick no bills'; drop the B

explanation.surface: Someone is sick of the headline having been taken off a poster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading' suggests a headline printed on the poster; it is just the first letter of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe someone unwell.

clue.text: Creek bank collapsed very fast

indicators.note: a collapsed structure is left in disorder

explanation.surface: The side of a creek gave way with alarming speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very fast' reads as describing how the bank collapsed; it is the definition, an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiomatic adjective for speed so great it risks a broken neck.

clue.text: Rebellious Chinese fighter

definitions.meaning: a member of the secret society behind the 1899-1901 anti-foreign rising in China
one who fights with fists in a ring

explanation.surface: A Chinese rebel who takes up arms.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one person described twice, and it is: a member of the Boxer Rebellion was called a Boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxer names both a member of the Chinese uprising and a prizefighter.

clue.text: Dance as training programme's ending

parts.note: qua = as, in the capacity of (Latin)

indicators.note: a word's ending is its final letter

explanation.surface: A dance is being used as the finale of a fitness regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' looks like a link between definition and wordplay; it supplies QUA, a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: The quadrille is a square dance for four couples.

clue.text: Point at which curse might end?

definitions.text: Point at which curse might end?

parts.note: the surface wants a moment in time; the setter means a punctuation point, a mark on the page
not a witch's hex being lifted but a swear word, which in print closes with a shout of punctuation

explanation.surface: Someone asks at what moment a spell or hex will finally lift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curse' suggests a witch's hex and 'point' a moment; the curse is a swear word, and the point is the punctuation that ends it on the page.
explanation.definitionFit: A written oath such as 'Damn!' ends with this point of punctuation.

clue.text: None buy farm, staggering many

indicators.note: a staggering person lurches about, letters reeling out of order

explanation.surface: An astonishing number of people are declining to buy a farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staggering many' reads as 'astonishingly many'; 'staggering' is the anagram signal and 'many' stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Any number of things means a great many of them.

clue.text: Scrap bell sounding thus

definitions.meaning: a scrap is a fight or heated row, British informal
the word imitating a bell's two-note chime

explanation.surface: An old bell has been sent for scrap metal, still ringing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' looks like a verb, to throw the bell out; it is a noun, a fight, which the British also call a ding-dong.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a noisy fight, and the imitative sound of a chiming bell.

clue.text: Comrade disrupted Conservative party's latest political arrangement

indicators.note: disrupted things are thrown out of order
the latest letter of a word is its last

explanation.surface: A leftist comrade has upset the Tories' newest political deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disrupted' looks like it acts on the Conservative party; it applies to all three pieces together.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: rule by the people is one system for arranging government.

clue.text: Some deny organisation put back barrier

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the phrase are used
the letters are taken in reverse order

parts.note: the run of letters d(ENY ORG)anisation

explanation.surface: Some people deny that an organisation reinstated a barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: A groyne is a low wall built out from a beach to stop sand washing away, common on British coasts.
explanation.definitionFit: A groyne is a sea barrier against erosion.

clue.text: Noble Spaniard turning up in Bahamas on vacation

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up means reading from bottom to top
the reversed word goes inside, as a guest is in a hotel
a vacated word is emptied, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: a señora is a Spanish woman

explanation.surface: A Spanish aristocrat appears holidaying in the Bahamas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noble Spaniard' reads as one person, a grandee; the Spaniard is only a SEÑORA to be reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun sense of 'noble': a titled woman of the lowest rank of the peerage.

clue.text: Poor attorney-general found in pool

indicators.note: one thing found in another is inside it

parts.note: a mere is a lake or pond

explanation.surface: A struggling Attorney-General is discovered in a swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pool' suggests swimming; a mere is a small lake, a word common in English place names.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain adjective synonym: both describe a scant, inadequate amount.

clue.text: Radical housing tax withdrawn

indicators.note: a word housing another gives it a home inside itself

parts.note: to tax someone is to tire them

explanation.surface: A radical levy on housing has been dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Housing tax' reads as a property levy; 'housing' is the container signal and 'tax' the verb, to wear out.
explanation.definitionFit: A retired or withdrawn person keeps to themselves.

clue.text: Feeble individual, male, riled Bob

indicators.note: stirred up, as in a riled sediment

parts.note: to bob down is to duck

explanation.surface: A weak man loses his temper at someone called Bob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a name; it is the verb, to duck down.
explanation.definitionFit: A lame duck is an ineffectual person or thing.

clue.text: Almost stop head abandoning opportunity to improve

indicators.note: almost all of the word, dropping its last letter
the first letter leaves the word

explanation.surface: A plea to nearly stop the boss walking away from a chance to get better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' reads as a boss walking out; it is the first letter of the word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: both mean to make something better.

clue.text: Republican apparently imprisoned over agreement

indicators.note: in a down answer, a word placed over another sits above it

parts.note: pen = enclosure, where one is shut in

explanation.surface: An American Republican appears to have been jailed over some deal.
explanation.walkthrough: A prenup (prenuptial agreement) is the contract a couple sign before marrying.
explanation.definitionFit: A prenup is an agreement settling property before a wedding.

clue.text: One with set routines, a nun maybe

definitions.meaning: someone who always does the same things
a nun is a being dressed in a religious robe; 'maybe' marks her as one example

explanation.surface: A nun, perhaps, as the model of a life run by fixed routines.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is playful: 'habit' shifts from custom to the nun's robe.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a person of fixed routine, read literally as a being clothed in a nun's robe.

clue.text: Stunner posed again, making comeback

indicators.note: coming back means running in the opposite direction

parts.note: a model who posed again resat

explanation.surface: A beautiful model posed once more, staging a return to the catwalk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stunner' is a beautiful woman on the surface, and a stun gun in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Taser is a weapon that stuns with an electric shock.

clue.text: Promise clubs US arenas will be renovated

indicators.note: renovating rebuilds, putting things in a new order

explanation.surface: Sports clubs pledge that American stadiums are going to be refurbished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubs' suggests sports teams; it is the card suit, one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain noun synonym: both are a firm pledge given to reassure someone.

clue.text: Brussels is backing petition

indicators.note: going backwards, so the letters read in reverse

parts.note: Brussels stands for the EU; 'is' is the 'S

explanation.surface: Brussels is supporting a petition.
explanation.walkthrough: Brussels, home of its institutions, stands for the European Union, EU; EU'S reads back as SUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb sense: to plead formally, as in begging for peace or bringing a claim to court.

clue.text: Food brought back for federal agents

indicators.note: returned the way it came, so reversed

parts.note: scran is British slang for food

explanation.surface: Takeaway food fetched back for a team of FBI officers.
explanation.walkthrough: Scran is northern British and naval slang for food. Narcs are US narcotics agents.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcs are American drug-enforcement officers, federal agents.

clue.text: Produce that is left in yard

indicators.note: the letters go in the other word, as goods go in a yard

explanation.surface: Garden vegetables have been left out in the yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Produce' looks like the noun, vegetables, and the answer can be a noun too: a crop's yield is its produce.
explanation.definitionFit: Yield means produce, as a verb or a noun.

clue.text: Is regarded as science fiction penned by out-of-date men

parts.note: OR = other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Science fiction written by old-fashioned men is judged in a particular way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penned by' reads as 'written by'; it means enclosed, as in a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb: to be accepted as something, often wrongly, is to be regarded as it.
